action: task-unit-queue-design-030-executor-loop-and-chains
reason: Owner direction of 2026-10-28 refining the task unit queue draft - the 15 minute cap is per unit (not per batch), the main agent's job becomes an executor loop that keeps executing tasks where needed, and a long activity such as Zombie Invasion keeps executing as a chain of units until its stop condition (zombies cleared) while other tasks ingest at unit boundaries when their time arrives. Design doc to version 0.3.0 - executor loop replaces the batch concept in sections 2 and 6, continuation chains and background priority 4 added, chain_id, chain_seq, attempts and max_attempts added to the unit schema, open questions 2 and 3 recorded as resolved by the owner, and one honest limit noted (the loop runs inside agent sessions and scheduled triggers, not as a literal daemon). tools/queue.py enforces the cap at enqueue (est_minutes above 15 refused), auto-numbers chain units, increments attempts on claim, and dead-letters a unit to done with status failed when attempts are exhausted on release or reap; stats gains per-chain done and pending counts. Self-tested in a scratch root - over-cap refusal, chain numbering, priority and expiry pick ahead of background units, and the third release dead-lettering the unit as failed. Live routine unchanged, still under owner review.

action: task-unit-queue-design-040-single-ticker
reason: Owner direction of 2026-10-28 simplifying the scheduling mechanism - the 3 segment schedules are retired in the design; a single regular ticker task (for example every 30 minutes) checks whether any tasks need to be executed, puts them into execution, and skips silently when there are none. Design doc to version 0.4.0 - section 6 now specifies the ticker (reap, produce idempotently from the tracker, execute the loop within a proposed 25 minute pass budget, silent skip), the device token as the overlap guard between ticks, bounded latency (one interval plus the remainder of the running unit, itself capped at 15 minutes), earliest-expiry picking, and the stats late list as the feedback signal for shortening the interval. Section 7 records that the segment field survives only as a reporting tag, and section 8 migration becomes shadow mode with the execute step disabled, then a single switch that deletes the segment crons and folds the Zombie Invasion rounds cron into chain production, then a settle period tuning only the interval and the pass budget. tools/queue.py needed no change - the ticker is composed entirely of its existing primitives (reap, enqueue, next, claim, complete, token, stats) plus the tracker due list.
